Question 01

Correct answerB

Work it through

  1. The word and identifies the intersection: 36 visitors both used a printed book and attended a workshop.
  2. The reference group is all 200 visitors, so use the grand total as the denominator.
  3. P(printed∩workshop)P\left(\text{printed} \cap \text{workshop}\right)P(printed∩workshop)=36200= \frac{36}{200}=20036​=0.18.= 0.18.=0.18. Thus 18% of all visitors had both characteristics.

Watch the reasoning

A uses only workshop attendees. C gives the proportion using printed books, whether or not they attended. D conditions on using a printed book.

Work it through

  1. Read each bar as a distribution within its membership group.
  2. The indoor portion for day members is between 60% and 70%. The indoor portion for evening members is between 40% and 50%. Thus the indoor proportion is greater for day members.

A changes a comparison of proportions into a comparison of counts. B pools the groups without their sizes. C misreads the evening bar, whose indoor portion is below 50%.

Stemplots and boxplots summarize quantitative values. A scatterplot requires two quantitative variables.

Work it through

  1. Probability describes the long-run relative frequency of an event under the stated random process.

Work it through

  2. The digits 0, 1, and 2 provide exactly three digits. The other seven digits represent packets without a rare seed.

Work it through
